properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 18 at 12:02PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...SUPER TYPHOON CHAMPI MOVING WEST-NORTHWEST AWAY FROM GUAM
COASTAL WATERS...
...A TROPICAL STORM WARNING AND TYPHOON WATCH ARE NO LONGER IN
EFFECT FOR TINIAN AND SAIPAN...

.NEW INFORMATION...
The Tropical Storm Warning and Typhoon Watch for Tinian and Saipan
are cancelled.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides important information and
recommended actions for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota.

Although tropical cyclone watches or warnings are not in effect
for Tinian and Saipan, possible impacts from related hazards are
still a concern.

A Flood Watch is in effect for portions of Guam and the Northern
Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that might
be in effect for your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 11 AM ChST, the center of Super Typhoon Champi (29W) was located
near latitude 13.1N, longitude 143.1E. This was about 115 miles
west-southwest of Guam. Storm motion was west-northwest, 290
degrees, at 14 mph. Storm intensity was 150 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Super Typhoon Champi continues to move west-northwestward as the eye
pulls away from Guam coastal waters, with its outermost rainbands
occasionally crossing the island. Sustained winds hover around or
just below damaging tropical storm-force late this morning, with
occasional Typhoon-force gusts to around 75 mph. Champi's eye, and
the destructive conditions within its compact eyewall, narrowly
missed Guam early this morning, passing just 10 miles south of the
southern tip of the island at around 4:26 AM ChST. The eye remains
compact and very well-defined, with a width of around 5 miles. The
islands of Tinian and Saipan are well outside of the radius of
sustained tropical-storm force conditions, but damaging gusts to 45
mph are still occurring. The Tropical Storm Warning, and Typhoon
Watch, are no longer in effect for Tinian and Saipan.

.PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...
properties.instruction:
As damaging tropical storm-force conditions continue, do not go
outside to check for damage or to implement temporary repairs,
even as sustained winds begin to diminish through the next few
hours. Occasional typhoon-force, or strong tropical storm-force
gusts, will maintain dangerous conditions outdoors. Do not open
the doors of your home or shelter until high winds fully subside.
Wait for the all-clear signal. Passing rain showers will bring
very strong gusts without warning.

properties.areaDesc: Ocracoke Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 17 at 8:33PM EDT until October 20 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, two to four feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 8 to 10 feet expected in the surf
zone. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents,
large breaking waves expected, and strong longshore currents
in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from midnight tonight to 8 PM EDT
Monday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday morning
through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level
is expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of
vehicles will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be
inundated, especially around high tide. There is a possibility
of being stranded on Ocracoke for multiple days. This could be
life threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or
surfer head first into the bottom causing neck and back
injuries. Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions. Strong longshore currents will create
dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash
impacts to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high
tide cycles into next week. Minor soundside water level rises
will also be possible.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

quickly away from the Marianas. Champi passed close to the southern
tip of Guam, less than 10 NM, as a strong Category 4 storm. Champi
is expected to strengthen further as it moves through the
Philippine Sea, possibly becoming a Category 5 super typhoon. Seas
are expected to remain hazardous through at least tonight, with
significant sea heights as high as 24 feet over western waters,
closest to Champi. Dangerous sea conditions may continue into
Monday.
properties.instruction:
Conditions will remain catastrophic for small craft, and extremely
dangerous for any vessels of larger size over western waters of Guam
and Rota. Waters will remain hazardous across the remainder of the
waters. Stay in safe harbor until the all clear is given.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 18 at 4:12AM ChST until October 18 at 6:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Guam, Rota.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris. Extensive street
flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Typhoon Champi (29W) will produce locally heavy rainfall late
tonight and Sunday, though expected rainfall has decreased
slightly as the larger rainbands remain mainly south and east of
the center of Champi. Rota could receive 3 to 5 inches, and Guam
might get 4 to 8 inches.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
